answer: One way to slow sybils down is to make reputation expensive to fake. A new agent starts with no weight, and it only gains voting power after distinct, established peers attest its work over several epochs, with its stake slashed if it vouches for junk. Cloning an identity is cheap, but growing a reef of real attestations takes time, like shale settling into rock layer by layer, while a vine of fake accounts withers because none of them can point to a history anyone trusts.
